defects: Seed 1, B-BARE: numerous long, straight scaffold branches end abruptly at substantial thickness, creating a conspicuous pole-like framework instead of the reference's progressively subdividing, tapering crown. B-WHOLE conceals much of this construction but retains exposed thick tips.

Seed 1, B-WHOLE: foliage forms predominantly upright, densely packed sprays around the shared framework. The references show more distinct spreading lateral masses and layered outer branching; the candidate lacks that defining crown organization.
Seed 1, both views: conspicuous repeated dark horizontal bark markings on the pale trunk differ from the reference's comparatively smooth gray bark and irregular surface mottling.
observations: The broad, rounded deciduous envelope is a supported partial match. Exact crown proportions and individual asymmetry can vary naturally.
The spruce anchor establishes stylized catalogue rendering as acceptable; photographic lighting, leaf-level realism and matching the photographs' backgrounds are unnecessary.
The left crown is clipped in both candidate views, so its complete outer silhouette remains unknown.
The photographs' specimen and condition relationships are undocumented. No seasonal or loading explanation is inferred.
No earlier candidate is supplied, so relative improvement cannot be assessed.

findings.observation: B-BARE reference_character, seed 1: fail. The visible framework contains repeated thick, abruptly ending straight limbs, especially across the upper crown. The bare reference shows a finer, progressively branching outer framework. Because B-WHOLE shares this geometry, foliage concealment does not resolve the construction artifact.

B-WHOLE reference_character, seed 1: fail. Upright foliage sprays dominate the crown rather than the spreading, layered lateral masses visible in the leafy references. B-BARE confirms the strong upward alignment of the supporting limbs. This is a structural character gap, not a requirement to reproduce an individual photographic silhouette.

The exposed trunk in both candidate views has repeated horizontal dark markings and a very pale surface. The bark reference instead supports smoother gray bark with irregular mottling. The repeated banding materially weakens the intended beech character.
The leafy candidate supports a broad, rounded deciduous crown with dense green foliage, consistent with the general envelope of the leafy beech references.
Simplified lighting, background and fine foliage rendering are compatible with the accepted catalogue anchor's stylized finish. These aspects do not independently block readiness.
